title: ci-cd-rollback-breadcrumbs-notes-11
content:
Context:
- Canary rollout for release-2026-02-28 (image: gcr.io/redwood-inference/inference-api:release-2026-02-28-abc123) started 2026-02-28 14:12 UTC. 10% traffic to canary via envoy-route /v1/generate (route weight).
- Observed spike in 5xx rates and token generation latency at ~14:25 UTC, coincident with warm-up of canary pods.
- Immediate mitigation: rolled canary back to stable image at 14:43 UTC (see actions below). Trying to capture breadcrumbs for postmortem and follow-ups.

Timeline / Actions taken (raw):
- 14:12 UTC: helm upgrade --install inference-api ./charts/inference-api --set image.tag=release-2026-02-28-abc123 --set canary.enabled=true --set canary.weight=10
- 14:20 UTC: kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=inference-api -o wide
  pod/inference-api-5f9d8c7f6-abcde  Ready 1/1  600Mi  node/gpu-1  14m
  pod/inference-api-canary-6b7f9d6d-xyz12  Ready 1/1  2Gi   node/gpu-3  2m
- 14:25 UTC: Alerts: svc-inference /v1/generate 5xx-rate > 3% (baseline 0.2%). P50 latency jumped from 75ms -> 820ms. P95 ~3.2s.
- 14:26 UTC: tail -n 200 /var/log/pods/inference-api-canary-6b7f9d6d/containers/inference-api.log
  ERROR [request-id=...) ModelRuntime error: kv-cache-miss TTL exceeded
  WARN  Retry loop triggered for request 5xx
  TRACE  gRPC connect failed: connection refused: dial tcp 10.42.3.11:50051: connect: connection refused
- 14:28 UTC: kubectl describe pod inference-api-canary-6b7f9d6d -n inference
  Events: BackOff  kubelet back-off restarting failed container
- 14:30 UTC: kubectl logs inference-api-canary-6b7f9d6d -c inference-api -n inference --previous
  OOMKilled in process model-worker (heap exceeded 4Gi)
- 14:35 UTC: Ran smoke curl -> 500 Internal Server Error from canary instances (consistent).
- 14:40 UTC: Attempted scaledown of canary -> kubectl scale deployment inference-api-canary --replicas=0 -n inference (no effect on error rate due to traffic still weighted).
- 14:43 UTC: Rollback command executed: helm rollback inference-api 2 --namespace inference (rollback to chart revision with image tag release-2026-02-21-9f7b2)
- 14:47 UTC: Confirmed route weight back to 0% canary, 100% stable via envoy control plane; 5xx rates returned to baseline by ~14:55 UTC.

Observed symptoms / logs (snippets):
- "ModelRuntime error: kv-cache-miss TTL exceeded" repeated 120x in 14:25-14:30 window.
- "connection refused: dial tcp 10.42.3.11:50051" from runtime-proxy -> suggests model worker process crashed or failed to bind.
- Kernel OOM messages in node/gpu-3 dmesg: "oom-killer invoked for pid 4321 (model-worker)", process rss ~4.3Gi.
- Envoy logs: "upstream 10.42.3.11:50051 response flags: UPR"
- Kube events: CrashLoopBackOff + BackOff on canary pod; stable pods unaffected.

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Canary image + runtime combination introduced increased memory usage (new quantization or new model binary) -> OOM in model-worker. (high confidence)
2) Incompatible changelog: orchestration or entrypoint changed to use different port (50052 vs 50051) -> connection refused. (medium)
3) Race in KV-cache init logic for cold-start path in the new runtime -> TTL errors and latency spikes (medium)
4) Node-specific issue (gpu-3 host had less allocatable memory due to noisy neighbor) -> but other pods on node looked normal; less likely. (low)
5) Canary config inadvertently set worker_count=4 leading to > memory footprint per pod -> config drift. (medium)

Commands and checks run locally (notes):
- docker inspect gcr.io/redwood-inference/inference-api:release-2026-02-28-abc123 | grep -i Entrypoint -A2 -> entrypoint is /usr/bin/inference-runtime --port=50051
- run image locally: docker run --entrypoint /bin/bash -it <image> then strace start -> nothing obvious.
- grepped git diff between release-2026-02-21 and release-2026-02-28 tags: git diff --name-only release-2026-02-21..release-2026-02-28 -> changes in model-loading, quantization-config.yaml, dockerfile bump of base image (ubuntu 22.04 -> 24.04).
- Reviewed PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/987: includes bump of CUDA libc and change to default model-worker threads to auto (was 2 -> now auto based on CPU). Suspect thread->memory growth.

Repro plan (next steps):
- Reproduce in staging with identical node type (gpu-3 equivalent). Steps:
  1) Deploy canary image to staging cluster with same helm values.
  2) Use load-generator to send traffic matching canary RPS and sequence length distribution (use test harness script : scripts/loadgen/canary-smoke.sh).
  3) Capture pod metrics (prometheus) for memory RSS, thread count, model-worker logs.
- Quick test: run container locally with reduced memory limit to see if OOM occurs: docker run --memory=3.5g ... and run deterministic sequence.
- Check quantization-config.yaml differences for any new memory-hungry options.
- Verify model binary sizes changed between tags: ls -lh models/ -> model.bin grew from 1.8G -> 2.6G. (suspect)

Rollback / Recovery notes (lessons learned):
- Helm rollback successfully restored stable traffic but the chart revision did not pin image digest; recommend using image.digest in chart values for future rollbacks to be deterministic.
- Envoy route weight rollback took ~4 min to converge due to control-plane batching; consider faster emergency path (direct route override).
- Need pre-deploy smoke tests that run quick memory-checks on new image (start container and run mem-profiling).

Action items / owners (todo):
- (Samira) Create staging reproduce run and attach profiling logs to ENG-3421. Due: 2026-03-03.
- (Evan) Add an image digest pin to Helm chart release pipeline. PR suggested: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-helm/pull/223. Due: 2026-03-05.
- (Diego) Add a pre-rollout smoke test that verifies basic RPC bind and < 3.5Gi RSS under N synthetic requests. Hook into CI for canary approval. Due: 2026-03-04.
- (Platform) Investigate whether the base image bump (Ubuntu 24.04 + libc) changed memory allocator behavior; reproduce with minimal container.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did only canary nodes hit OOM? (config or image specific?)
- Did the model binary change (size + loading behavior) between tags require more memory at cold start?
- Is there a regression introduced by thread auto-scaling in PR #987? Could force-setting WORKER_THREADS=2 mitigate?

Notes-to-self / scratch ideas:
- Consider adding a canary resource buffer: e.g., temporarily increase memory limits for canary pods during rollout warmup to avoid OOM while we observe.
- Add a GRACE_PERIOD / startup-probe to env proxy to reduce 502/UPR noise during warmup.
- Postmortem must include timeline, command list, and recommended CI gating for memory/peak RSS.

Relevant artifacts / refs: ENG-3421 (incident), PR 987 (platform changes), infra-helm PR 223 (image digest), slack thread https://app.slack.com/client/T12345/C67890?thread_ts=1700000000.000200

Raw commands to reproduce locally (note):
- docker run -it --rm --memory=3.5g -p 50051:50051 gcr.io/redwood-inference/inference-api:release-2026-02-28-abc123 /usr/bin/inference-runtime --port=50051
- scripts/loadgen/canary-smoke.sh --host localhost --port 50051 --rps 50 --seq-dist long --duration 300s

Capture checklist for staging run:
- prometheus metrics: container_memory_rss_bytes, process_open_fds, process_threads
- pprof snapshot from model-worker at t=30s, 90s, 5min
- dmesg for OOM kill messages
- kube events and pod logs (previous + current)

--- end of scratch notes ---
